reply.result:
**Question:** Does the service need to serve overlapping requests at the same time, or may it finish one request before starting the next?

**Why it matters:** The Assumptions section promises that a read never sees a half-written snippet but never says whether two callers can be in flight at once — which decides both whether the storage layer needs protection against simultaneous access and whether one stalled caller can stall everybody.

**Recommended:** Option B — serving requests concurrently costs essentially nothing in a standard library HTTP server, and it removes a real hazard for a service people pipe into scripts: under Option A a single caller that opens a connection and stops sending blocks every other caller until it times out. The obligation it adds (each snippet written so that it becomes visible complete or not at all) is one the spec already commits to.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Serve one request at a time; later callers wait their turn. Requires a read timeout so a stalled caller cannot block the service indefinitely |
| B | Serve overlapping requests concurrently, with each snippet written so that a concurrent reader sees it either complete or not at all, and a concurrent delete never yields a partial read |
| C | Leave it to the implementation and record it as an assumption |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
